name: Handy
description: A free, open source, and extensible speech-to-text application that works completely offline.
one_liner: Free software that turns your voice into typed text in any app on your computer, entirely offline — hold a key, talk, and your words appear where your cursor is.
buyer: A privacy-conscious professional (writer, lawyer, support agent) who wants dictation that never sends audio to the cloud, and doesn't want to pay for a commercial dictation subscription.
business_use_cases: A writer or journalist drafts articles by voice entirely offline, keeping unpublished work off any third-party server.
A support team deploys it company-wide as a free dictation tool instead of paying per-seat for a commercial transcription SaaS.
An accessibility-focused nonprofit recommends and supports it for users who need hands-free text input but can't afford paid tools.

money_ideas.idea: Paid enterprise support and deployment (MDM profiles, fleet updates) for companies rolling it out to many machines.
A paid companion app with custom vocabularies/macros for specific professions (legal, medical dictation shortcuts).

steal_this: Build a thin paid layer of profession-specific vocabulary packs and text-replacement macros (legal terms, medical shorthand) on top of the free core app.
